item.title: UFC’s Conor McGregor takes a cheeky dig at Merab Dvalishvili-Usman Nurmagomedov hotel clash
item.description: UFC’s Conor McGregor takes a cheeky dig at Merab Dvalishvili-Usman Nurmagomedov hotel clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Recently, former UFC Champion Merab Dvalishvili was attacked by a group headed by fellow MMA fighter Usman Nurmagomedov in Abu Dhabi, UAE. The attack reminded fans of the past bus incident between Conor McGregor and Khabib Nurmagomedov. A few years ago, ahead of their UFC 229 fight, McGregor and Nurmagomedov got into one of the most memorable MMA feuds of all time . Both the fighters got very personal with each other and shared shots outside of the octagon. Dvalishvili is in Abu Dhabi ahead of this Saturday’s RAF event and later uploaded a video of his bloodied face on social media and explained the incident. Multiple videos of the incident started going viral on social media, which showed Nurmagomedov ambushing Dvalishvili. The Georgian fighter has a long history with the Nurmagomedov family and had once defeated Umar in 2025. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In his usual Conor manners, McGregor joined in and started having fun. McGregor responded to the hotel lobby fight in Abu Dhabi by sharing a photoshopped picture on Instagram that humorously mocked Ilia Topuria and alluded to McGregor’s notorious 2018 bus assault on Khabib Nurmagomedov’s team. The Ilia Topuria involvement in McGregor’s meme is not incidental and was done purposely, after Topuria shared his thoughts on the ambush. “Usman has reportedly been detained, along with the cowards who were with him. “And these are the same people who dare to preach about humility and respect? What a disgrace. A bunch of absolute cowards. I always thought you were a bunch of mediocre individuals. Now you’ve removed every last doubt. Honor, respect, and humility aren’t words you preach. They’re values you live by. And you’ve shown none of them,” Topuria earlier wrote while responding to the viral video. As of now, neither the UFC nor RAF have officially commented on the incident. View this post on Instagram Related: UFC’s Merab Dvalishvili ambushed by Usman Nurmagomedov and group in Abu Dhabi Related: UFC veteran slams Jake Hager for Power Slap: ‘This is the dumbest thing’

item.title: Aaryavir Sehwag's old video of interviewing Virat Kohli goes viral amid U19 Asia Cup heroics - Watch
item.description: Almost nine years after interviewing Virat Kohli as a young child, Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India cricketer Virender Sehwag, is back in the spotlight, this time for his performances on the cricket field. A video of his 2017 interaction with Kohli has resurfaced on social media after the son of former India opener Virender Sehwag scored 160 in the Under-19 Asia Cup. Aaryavir was a child when he interviewed Kohli, who was then India's captain across all three formats, for Star Sports. Since then, he has taken his first steps in age-group cricket and is now making a name for himself with the bat. On Tuesday, the 19-year-old played a key role in India's 70-run win over the UAE, which secured their place in the semi-finals. Aaryavir scored 160 off 168 balls, hitting 17 fours and seven sixes. He also shared a 193-run partnership with VK Vineeth, who scored 67, as India posted 309 for seven. Following his innings, the video of his interaction with Kohli from 2017 started doing the rounds on social media. The interview offered a glimpse into Aaryavir's admiration for the former India captain. During the conversation, Aaryavir asked Kohli about his first meeting with Virender Sehwag. Kohli recalled meeting the former India opener in Delhi through a state-level coach who knew both of them. The meeting took place after Kohli had scored his first double century in Under-17 cricket. Aaryavir also brought up a photograph of Ashish Nehra presenting a trophy to Kohli when the latter was a teenager. He asked Kohli how it felt to later have Nehra play under his captaincy. "This is why I say this: Always think, 'I can do it'," said Kohli. — StarSportsIndia (@StarSportsIndia) Kohli also spoke about his journey in cricket and encouraged Aaryavir to dream big and have faith in his abilities. The 160 against the UAE was Aaryavir's maiden Youth ODI century. He had also scored an unbeaten 72 against Nepal earlier in the tournament. Sehwag's role will also be key in the semi-final of the U19 Asia Cup, where India are bowling first against Afghanistan. FOLLOW LIVE

item.title: Sam Bennett Sparks Florida Panthers’ Offense
item.description: Credit: James Carey Lauder-Imagn Images When the Florida Panthers needed an offensive spark to snap a two-game losing streak, veteran forward Sam Bennett delivered in a big way. In a decisive 4-1 road win over the Columbus Blue Jackets at Nationwide Arena on Tuesday night, Bennett netted two goals, propelling Florida’s record to 10-7-2 and injecting fresh momentum into a roster grappling with early-season injuries. Finding His Scoring Touch After a sluggish start to the 2026-27 campaign, Bennett has quickly rediscovered his scoring touch, tallying four goals in his last five games. Against Columbus, his knack for capitalizing in critical moments proved to be the difference-maker. Following a scoreless opening period, Bennett wasted no time breaking the ice in the second frame. Just two minutes in, he converted on the Panthers’ first power play of the game. Anton Lundell navigated through traffic in the neutral zone and delivered a perfect feed to Bennett, who unleashed a shot past Blue Jackets goalie Cam Talbot . This goal not only got Florida on the board but also extended their streak of games with a power-play goal to seven of their last eight contests. Later in the third period, with Columbus trailing 2-1 and pushing for an equalizer, Bennett showcased his composure under pressure. During a 4-on-4 sequence—sparked by roughing penalties to Matthew Tkachuk and Adam Fantilli —Bennett seized the opportunity, carrying the puck into the offensive zone and firing a slick wrist shot from the faceoff dot just under the crossbar. This insurance marker restored Florida’s two-goal cushion and effectively sealed the victory. A Complete Team Effort While Bennett provided the primary offensive punch, he received ample support across the lineup as reported by Yahoo Sports : Goaltending Excellence: Jacob Markström anchored the defensive effort, turning aside 37 of 38 shots, including three critical saves during a third-period Columbus power play, despite facing a 38-28 shot disadvantage. Franchise Milestones: Lars Eller doubled Florida’s lead in the second period with a sharp feed from Carter Verhaeghe , while Sam Reinhart iced the contest with an empty-netter, marking his 199th goal with the franchise and moving him past Jonathan Huberdeau for second place on the Panthers’ all-time goals list. Family History: By assisting on Bennett’s third-period goal, Matthew Tkachuk extended his active point streak to five games and his personal streak against Columbus to 16 consecutive outings. This achievement places him alongside his father, Hockey Hall of Famer Keith Tkachuk , as the first father-son duo in NHL history to each record a point streak of at least 15 games against the same franchise. A Complete Team Effort While Bennett provided the primary offensive punch, he received ample support across the lineup as reported by Yahoo Sports : Goaltending Excellence: Jacob Markström anchored the defensive effort, turning aside 37 of 38 shots, including three critical saves during a third-period Columbus power play, despite facing a 38-28 shot disadvantage. With key stars nearing a return and Bennett heating up offensively, the Panthers will return home to Amerant Bank Arena on Thursday night to host the division-rival Detroit Red Wings before heading out for back-to-back road matchups against St. Louis and Dallas . If Bennett can maintain this scoring pace, Florida will be well-positioned to climb the Atlantic Division standings as their lineup returns to full strength.

item.title: ‘I’m Not Done Yet’ – Nong-O’s Hunger For Greatness Burns Bright Ahead Of ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix
item.description: Former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion Nong-O Hama has captured almost every major accolade the sport has to offer, but the 40-year-old striking icon is far from finished writing his legacy. He returns to action at The Inner Circle 38 to face Rodtang “The Iron Man” Jitmuangnon in a highly anticipated quarterfinal clash of the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix. Their marquee all-Thai showdown takes place at Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, November 13. Subscribers can catch the action exclusively at live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram As an eight-time ONE World Champion and four-time Lumpinee Stadium Muay Thai World Champion, Nong-O has firmly secured his place on the Mount Rushmore of striking greats. Yet beyond the glittering trophy case is a martial artist with plenty more to prove. One More Chapter Few fighters have enjoyed a sustained peak quite like Nong-O’s, but the decorated Thai veteran knows that past achievements count for little when a fresh challenge awaits. The Grand Prix has assembled eight of the planet’s most elite flyweights , with a fascinating generational contrast running directly through the ultra-competitive bracket. Having already achieved absolute dominance on the global stage, the opportunity to add another unique distinction to his resume is one he deeply relishes. Nong-O told onefc.com: “The fact that the World Grand Prix winner gets two belts is awesome. I’ve already won the gold belt, and it felt amazing. Now, I really want that silver belt to sit right next to my gold one. I’m going to give it everything I’ve got to make it happen.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Standing between Nong-O and that ultimate ambition, however, is a field packed with considerably younger challengers. For context, the 40-year-old is exactly twice the age of the tournament’s youngest participant, 20-year-old Ramadan “The Scorpion” Ondash . Some critics may question whether his finest days are safely in the rearview mirror, but the Evolve MMA and Superbon Training Camp representative insists his internal competitive fire burns as hot as ever. Nong-O added: “I don’t put too much thought [about my age]. I still train the same, take care of my body the same, and manage to go all-out in fight camp. I have the exact same hunger and drive I had when I was 20 or 25. I’m not done yet. “The rest of the participants are all young, fresh, and pack heavy power. But I’m not letting that get to me. My job is to train to the absolute limit, fight with everything I have, and win every single match [until I get the belts].” View this post on Instagram The Reasons That Keep Him Fighting Beyond the championship hardware and public adulation, Nong-O’s greatest motivation is profoundly personal. Even at this late stage of his career, the Bangkok-based warrior remains entirely committed to finding new ways to sharpen his tools and stay one step ahead of the evolving competition. He explained: “What I have now over my younger self is definitely experience – years of reading fights and adapting on the fly. Lately, I’ve also been putting extra focus on building up my physical strength and power.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Source

item.title: Rob Gronkowski answers whether the Patriots’ season is over if they lose to the Lions
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images The New England Patriots have had a mixed 2026/27 season so far, leaving them with a 5-4 record ahead of their Week 10 tie. They were most recently beaten 45-27 by the Green Bay Packers and look pretty unlikely to catch the 7-1 Buffalo Bills, who are top of the AFC East, especially if they lose this weekend. New England will face off with the Detroit Lions on Sunday and Rob Gronkowski has now been asked how important that game is for his former team’s season. When he appeared on Kay Adams’ show this week, she asked Gronkowski: “If they lose [to the Lions], this season, is it a wrap?” Gronkowski replied by making it clear he does not think their season is over and suggested they can still make the Wild Card. He responded: “It’s not a wrap if they lose this game. They’re still 5-5, they’re still going to be in second place in their division. “The Jets, the Miami [Dolphins], they don’t have a chance. They can still beat up on those two teams as well throughout the season. But I feel like they can definitely get in as a Wild Card still. There’s no question about that. “5-5. The Detroit Lions, you know, they’re a good team so if they lose to them… But you know, you can’t just say the season is a wrap. Not at all.” The Patriots last reached the Super Bowl in 2025/26, where they lost to the Seattle Seahawks, and have not won the showpiece since 2018. item.title: Official | Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage
item.description: Official | Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage Crystal Palace have confirmed the sacking of Pierre Sage. The Frenchman joined the South London club back in the summer from RC Lens. He is now linked with a return to the Ligue 1 club. Sage led Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 and to a maiden Coupe de France triumph. He had preveiously spoken of a dream to manage in the Premier League and it is Crystal Palace who provided that opportunity. However, Oliver Glasner’s successor at Selhurst Park has struggled. In 10 games, he has managed just two wins and one draw. Heading into the international break, Crystal Palace sit bottom of the Premier League. The club’s directors have, therefore, decided to call time on the Frenchman’s reign. He managed just 16 games in all competitions. His assistants, Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa, and Sandy Guichard have left with him Crystal Palace have confirmed that a successor will be announced in due course. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Pierre Sage sacked by Crystal Palace
item.description: Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage after the club slumped to bottom of the Premier League table for the first time since December 2017. The Frenchman moved to Selhurst Park on a three-year contract this summer after an impressive year at Lens, where he led the club to a runner-up finish in Ligue 1, won the Coupe de France and Trophee des Champions titles for the first time, and qualified for the Champions League. But he was unable to replicate that success across his 16 games in all competitions at Palace, who have conceded the most goals of any top-flight side this season and claimed just seven points out of a possible 30 during his tenure, and sit two points off safety going into the November international break. A club statement released on Thursday said: “Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager. “The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future. “An update on the process of appointing a new Manager will be provided in due course.” Former Brentford and Tottenham manager Thomas Frank could be considered as Palace now attempt to rescue themselves from a relegation fight, while former Burnley, Everton and Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche is also out of work and would be available. Three members of Sage’s coaching staff, Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard, have also departed. Sage leaves after a 3-1 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park, which marked Palace’s fourth straight league loss and seventh in the top-flight this season. Palace also have one win, two draws and one defeat from four Europa League games and are through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup, where they play Sunderland next month. The former Lyon boss had replaced perhaps the most successful Crystal Palace manager in modern history in Oliver Glasner , who won the FA Cup and Conference League with the Eagles before moving to Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest at the end of last season.

item.title: PSV hoping to bring Kevin De Bruyne to Eindhoven in January
item.description: PSV hoping to bring Kevin De Bruyne to Eindhoven in January HLN are reporting that PSV are looking to bring Kevin De Bruyne to the Eredivisie in January. The former Manchester City midfielder is in the final season of his contract with Napoli and, according to the Belgian paper, is open to a move to PSV. This will certainly put other clubs on alert, especially Belgian sides who may look to persuade the Belgian captain to return to his home country for the final move of his career. De Bruyne came through the Genk academy and played over 100 games for the club before moving to Chelsea in 2012. After a loan spell with Werder Bremen, De Bruyne never got a real chance to prove himself in London and was sold to Wolfsburg in January 2014. With 20 goals in 73 games, De Bruyne really showed his quality in Germany and helped the Wolves win the DFB Pokal. In 2015 he left for Manchester City where he showed himself to be one of the best creative midfielders in world football. After over 400 appearances and 100 goals for the Citizens, he left to join Napoli on a free transfer in 2025. Things have not gone as well as De Bruyne would have hoped in Serie A, and after nine goals in 36 games it appears he is happy to end his time in Italian football. PSV appear to be leading the race, but expect other clubs to become interested if it is clear that De Bruyne will move in January. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: Merab Dvalishvili jumped by Khabib Nurmagomedov’s cousin to spark hotel brawl
item.description: Merab Dvalishvili was jumped by Usman Nurmagomedov to spark a brawl in an Abu Dhabi hotel, leaving the former UFC champion bloodied and bruised. Dvalishvili was filming an interview when PFL lightweight champion Nurmagomedov, the cousin of legendary former UFC fighter Khabib, walked up to the bantamweight from behind before slapping him. The Georgian looked stunned by the initial attack but as Nurmagomedov’s team came in with follow-up shots, a huge fight between the two fighters and their respective entourages broke out in the hotel lobby. Merab Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised after being jumped by Usman Nurmagomedov in a hotel lobby (Merab Dvalishvili/Instagram) Dvalishvili took to social media after the altercation to brand Russia’s Nurmagomedov and his team “snakes”, posting a video of himself receiving treatment for his injuries. He said: “What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. “What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way. “You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***?” Dvalishvili, 35, is due to wrestle at a Real American Freestyle (RAF) event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday, taking on Brazilian Marlon Moraes. He previously fought and beat Nurmagomedov’s older brother, Umar, to retain the UFC bantamweight title in an enthralling fight in 2025, with Dvalishvili branding his opponent “spoiled” in the build-up. Former two-weight UFC champion Ilia Topuria , a friend of Dvalishvili who also fights out of Georgia, blasted Nurmagomedov and his attackers as he reacted to the footage of the fracas on X. He wrote: "Usman has reportedly been detained, along with the cowards who were with him. Usman Nurmagomedov (right) with cousin Khabib (centre) in his corner (PFL MMA) "What a disgrace. A bunch of absolute cowards. I always thought you were a bunch of mediocre individuals. Now you've removed every last doubt. "Honour, respect, and humility aren't words you preach. They're values you live by. And you've shown none of them." Middleweight champion Sean Strickland commented on Dvalishvili’s Instagram post calling for a “lifetime ban” for everyone involved, while Irish lightweight Paul Hughes - who took Nurmagomedov to his limit across two PFL title fights - lambasted his former rival and called his team out for similar behaviour in the past. “Utterly disgusting,” Hughes wrote. “The same people assaulted my supporters in Dubai for no reason. “How can this team ever speak about humility and respect. And yet there will be no repercussions.” Merab Dvalishvili beat Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's brother, in January 2025 (Getty) UFC lightweight champion and pound-for-pound kingpin Islam Makhachev , however, issued a rebuttal in defence of Nurmagomedov and suggested that a previous altercation between the two camps, before an RAF event in July, sparked Wedne

item.title: ‘I’m not looking past him’: Azim vs Gabriel Valenzuela set for December 4
item.description: Adam Azim is officially set for his next outing, as a December 4 fight against Gabriel Valenzuela at the Copper Box is now formally on the schedule. During an appearance for the opening presser, Azim would share his thoughts on being relatively inactive this year and his expectations to get things back on track. Here’s some of what he had to say below. Azim on facing Valenzuela “Gabriel Valenzuela is a great opponent, very tricky, quite awkward, can punch as well. I’m not looking past him. He’s fought some great fighters like Delgado, Subriel Matias, and yeah, I’m going to put on a great performance December 4th and look very good. “…at the end of the day I’m at the [cusp] of becoming world champion and I ain’t looking past him.” On how he would assess his 2026 campaign “Of course it’s been frustrating, being in camp for a very long time. I had an injury, had to pull out. But everything happens for a reason. I’m going to have my second fight in December and hopefully next year I’m going to be out three times. “At the end of the day, like next year I want to be active as much as I want. I want to fight in January, I want to fight in like July, and then December or something. But I want to fight Dalton Smith next year. And hopefully I’m on the [cusp] to become a world champion and hopefully me and him can make it happen.” On his world title aspirations “I’m in a grateful for the position I’m in now. Hopefully, have this fight with flying colors and hopefully go into a world title fight. I think that’s my plan.” On believing he’s the A-side over Dalton Smith “140 is a great division and hopefully once I have a world title then I’ve got a lot of opportunities — I’ve got Shakur, I’ve got Dalton, I’ve got like Antuanne Russell. There’s loads of names in the division but I’m not looking past Gabriel Valenzuela first.”

item.title: RB Leipzig star boasts better scoring rate than Mbappé and Kane
item.description: RB Leipzig star boasts better scoring rate than Mbappé and Kane After missing the start of the season through injury, RB Leipzig star Rômulo has made an impressive return, showing remarkable efficiency in front of goal in the Bundesliga. The Brazilian forward needed just one shot to take his Bundesliga tally to five goals for the season in last week's 5-2 win over Augsburg. He has spent just 397 minutes on the pitch to score those five goals, averaging a goal every 79 minutes, or 1.13 goals per 90 minutes. That puts him ahead of Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé, who has averaged 1.09 goals per 90 minutes in La Liga this season, and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, who has managed 0.50 in the Bundesliga. Rômulo has also been remarkably clinical in front of goal, converting five of his 11 shots in the Bundesliga this season for an impressive rate of 45.5 percent. To put that into perspective, Raphinha (FC Barcelona) and Mbappé have conversion rates of 39.5 and 20.3 percent respectively in La Liga, while Kane has converted 9.3 percent of his shots in the Bundesliga. Having also scored in a 4-5 friendly defeat to Mladá Boleslav on Thursday, the 24-year-old will be looking to maintain his impressive form in front of goal when RB Leipzig travel to face Union Berlin on November 21 following the international break.

item.title: Arsenal youngster signs new contract
item.description: Arsenal youngster signs new contract Arsenal youth goalkeeper Jack Talbot has put pen to paper on a professional contract, the club have now confirmed. Photo via Arsenal.com Arsenal youngster Jack Talbot has signed a professional contract with the club, extending his stay in north London. The goalkeeper joined Arsenal at eight years old in 2017, and his new deal is set to take him to a full decade with the club and beyond. In that time, Talbot has worked his way up to the u18s, making 14 appearances for the Gunners in the u18 Premier League. He’s also featured on the bench for the u19s in the UEFA Youth League, and for the u21s in the Premier League 2, but he’s yet to debut in either competition. “It’s a very special day for me and family,” Talbot said of the new deal. “I’ve been at the club for a long time, so to be here now signing my professional contract is obviously a very proud moment for me and my family. “Definitely a lot of ups and downs, a lot of learning over the 10, 11 years that I’ve been here, but the main message is just work hard, keep believing in yourself and eventually you’ll get to where you want to be.” Photo via Arsenal.com Talbot hasn’t had the easiest start to the season, following up an opening-day clean sheet with a red card in his third appearance back in August, and suffering an injury upon his return from suspension against Tottenham Hotspur last month. The timing of that injury was particularly unfortunate, as substitute goalkeeper Maximiliano Lo Presti also went on to get injured in the same game, forcing midfielder Emerson Nwaneri to play in goal . But Arsenal ended up taking all three points anyway, with Mylo Bernard netting a 97th-minute winner. Photo via Arsenal.com Given those setbacks, Talbot will be pleased to go into the November international break on the positive note of a new contract. At 18, he’s had to wait a while for a pro deal, having first become eligible for one last September. Now that it’s confirmed, he can focus on his football again. image via Arsenal

item.title: Gary Neville fumes at ‘classless’ Man Utd handling of Michael Carrick
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester United manager Michael Carrick pictured prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Gary Neville fumes at ‘classless’ Man Utd handling of Michael Carrick») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Gary Neville has branded Manchester United “classless” over their actions in the days before Michael Carrick’s sacking. Carrick’s departure from the club was finally announced on Thursday morning and the Press Association understands Mauricio Pochettino has been lined up to replace him. Official confirmation of Carrick’s sacking came after a period of limbo for the former United midfielder, who had reported to Carrington again on Thursday after taking training on Tuesday and Wednesday amid reports he would be removed from his role. His fate was sealed the day after a meeting took place between the club’s powerbrokers in Monaco, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada travelled to see co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Speaking on the Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast, which was recorded prior to Thursday’s confirmation, former United defender Neville said the process feels “clumsy”. He said: “We’re sat here today recording this programme knowing that Michael Carrick is going to be sacked tomorrow, knowing that they’re speaking to Mauricio Pochettino, knowing that they’ve spoken to (Julian) Nagelsmann, (Eddie) Howe – and they should be doing that by the way, I’m not saying they shouldn’t be doing that… “But I think the fact they’re in Monaco now and they can’t sack him today knowing that it’s happening, to me it just feels a little bit clumsy, it feels a little bit classless. “I think if you live in Monaco, you can’t leave a guy hanging for 24 or 48 hours just because you live in Monaco, that can’t happen.” In May, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis until 2028 having taken interim charge in January, but the club have struggled so far this term. United are in the Premier League relegation zone with just eight points having won only one of their 10 league matches this season. Pochettino has previously managed Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea before becoming United States head coach and Neville praised the Argentinian for the physical fitness instilled within his teams. “One thing we do know about him is he does run his players, he does put physical fitness really at the top of the agenda. item.description: RALEIGH, NC - NOVEMBER 07: Runningback Nate Sheppard #20 of the Duke Blue Devils evades a tackle attempt from inside linebacker Jordan Moreta #44 of the NC State Wolfpack during the college football game between the NC State Wolfpack and the Duke Blue Devils on November 7, 2026 at Carter-Finley Stadium in Raleigh, North Carolina. Television coverage will be provided by ABC. Miami is ranked number seven in the College Football Playoff Rankings and the ‘Canes are currently favored by 13.5 points. Duke is riding a three-game win streak and has outscored their last two opponents 88-5, while Miami is coming off a 31-24 loss at Notre Dame. Duke and Miami have played one common opponent. Miami defeated North Carolina 38-35, while Duke lost to North Carolina 24-20. Both games were played in Chapel Hill. This is the third consecutive meeting in the series where the game will be played in Miami. Miami beat Duke 53-31 in 2024, while Duke beat Miami 45-21 in 2022. Injury Report: There are no unexpected additions to the injury report for Duke. Safety Patrick Smith-Young and offensive lineman Cole Allen underwent surgery, after suffering injuries in the N.C. State game, and are out for the season. The main injury for Miami is wide receiver Malachi Toney who remains out with an ankle injury. Toney is a Heisman Trophy candidate and one of, if not the, most explosive players in college football. Offense: Miami’s offense is a juggernaut, ranked number one in the ACC in scoring, total and passing offense, and number two in rushing offense. Quarterback Darian Mensah is one of the best quarterbacks in the nation and even without Toney the ‘Canes have an abundance of playmakers. Duke Coach Manny Diaz on Miami’s offense without star wide receiver Malachi Toney: “Anytime you play Miami it still comes down to stopping the run, big physical offensive line, backs that fall forward. Duke leads the ACC in scoring, total and rushing defense, and is fourth in passing defense. Duke has sacked the opponent’s quarterback 26 times. Coach Diaz is aggressive with the blitz package. Players to Watch: Darian Mensah, Mark Fletcher, Jr., Cooper Barkate, Javian Mallory Defense: Miami is ranked number one in the ACC in rushing defense,but number 16 in passing defense. While opponents average only 64.3 rushing yards per game, they pass for 259.3 yards per game. The Blue Devils pass game has really started to click the past few weeks and it will need to click on Saturday in Miami. Quarterback Walker Eget is becoming more and more comfortable in the offense and with the receivers. Offensive coordinator Jonathan Brewer: “I can feel the flow of the offense, especially the passing game, something we have been slowly building toward the last three weeks. We’ve been moving the ball up and down the field, throwing the football, which opens things up for us, especially … the run game, really lightened the box.” Forcing defenses to lighten the box is critical when your running back is the explosive Nate Sheppard who leads the nation in total touchdowns and total points scored, at 21 and 126 respectively. Look for Duke to be creative in getting Sheppard the ball for opportunities to impact the game. Linebacker Mohamed Toure leads the ‘Canes with 56 tackles and defensive lineman Marquise Lightfoot has recorded seven sacks. Miami has intercepted four passes this season and recovered six fumbles. Miami also has a plus five turnover margin, which is tied for 23rd in the nation. Miami’s defense will try to utilize their big defensive line to shut down the run game and make Duke one dimensional, but that is easier planned than accomplished. Players to Watch: Marquise Lightfoot, Mohamed Toure, Justin Scott Prediction: The Blue Devils defense steps up with another big performance and controls Miami’s run game as Duke pulls off the big upset. Duke 21, Miami 17. Go to the DBR Boards to find Blue Healer Auctions || Drop us a line

item.title: How does Carrick's record compare to other Man Utd managers?
item.description: [Getty Images] Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United after only 32 games in charge. Including Ralf Rangnick's six month spell as caretaker manager, United have now been through eight permanent managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. Despite managing to rescue their season and finish third in the 2025-26 Premier League, United have since endured their worst start to a season in 40 years and are in the relegation zone after only one win in 10 matches. Carrick ranks sixth out of eight managers for win ratio (47%) at Manchester United in all competitions since Ferguson retired (not including his two games as caretaker in 2021). However, during his tenure Carrick produced United's best points per game ratio (1.74) since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (1.81), ranking him third out of eight managers. Including Ralf Rangnick's six month spell as caretaker manager, United have now been through eight permanent managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. Despite managing to rescue their season and finish third in the 2025-26 Premier League, United have since endured their worst start to a season in 40 years and are in the relegation zone after only one win in 10 matches. Carrick ranks sixth out of eight managers for win ratio (47%) at Manchester United in all competitions since Ferguson retired (not including his two games as caretaker in 2021). However, during his tenure Carrick produced United's best points per game ratio (1.74) since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (1.81), ranking him third out of eight managers. So how does his time in charge compare to other managers at Old Trafford? How does his record compare? Ruben Amorim Ruben Amorim departed Old Trafford only 10 months ago [Getty Images] Period in charge: November 2024-January 2026 Number of games: 63 Win percentage: 38% Trophies: None Ruben Amorim departed the club after 14 months in charge . In the 63 games under his tenure, United won 24 matches, drew 18 and lost on 21 occasions - earning the 40-year-old Portuguese the unfortunate record of the worst win ratio (38%) of any permanent United boss. His record of 1.23 points per game in the Premier League was the lowest of all managers at Old Trafford since the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson. Amorim also had the worst goals conceded per game ratio in the league (1.53) and the lowest league clean sheet ratio (15%) of any United manager. They finished 15th in Amorim's first season in charge and also reached the Europa League final, where they lost 1-0 to Tottenham in Bilbao. Erik ten Hag Erik ten Hag won two trophies during his time in charge of Manchester United [Getty Images] Period in charge: May 2022-October 2024 Number of games: 128 Win percentage: 54.7% Trophies: Two Erik ten Hag took charge of Manchester United for more than two years - winning 70 of the 128 games played under his leadership. Their win ratio in the Premier League during that time was 51.8% - the third highest of permanent managers at the club since Ferguson. He guided United to a third place finish in his first season and earned their first piece of silverware in six seasons with a 2-0 win against Newcastle in the 2023 Carabao Cup final. He also took the Red Devils to the FA Cup final, losing 2-1 to rivals Manchester City during that campaign. The Dutchman made amends by beating City in the following season's FA Cup final, but Ten Hag was sacked after a poor start to the 2024-25 season, ending with 1.72 points per game during his tenure. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Period in charge: December 2018-November 2021 Number of games: 168 Win percentage: 54.2% Trophies: Zero Former forward Ole Gunnar Solskjaer became the club's 25th manager in December 2018. Solskjaer oversaw a win rate of 54.2% as his side won 91 of the 168 games played across all competitions. The Norwegian had a 51.4% win ratio in the top-flight, but his failure to earn silverware and challenge for the title proved to be his undoing. United reached the semi-final of the FA Cup in his second season in charge and also reached the Europa League final a year later. He recorded his best league finish of second in 2020-21. But Solskjaer departed in November 2021 after a run of just one win in seven Premier League games. Jose Mourinho Manchester United's win percentage under Jose Mourinho was 58.3% [Getty Images] Period in charge: May 2016-December 2018 Number of games: 144 Win percentage: 58.3% Trophies: Three Jose Mourinho managed Manchester United for two and a half years between May 2016 and December 2018. During Mourinho's leadership, the club had a win rate of 58.3% across all competitions, winning 84 of the 144 games played - the highest percentage since Ferguson's reign. In the Premier League, his win ratio was 53.8%, again the highest since Ferguson. His side's points per game was 1.89 in the Premier League. Mourinho won the Community Shield and the Europa League in his first season. In the 2017-18 season, his side finished second, but lost the 2018 FA Cup final to Chelsea. Mourinho was sacked in his third year of leadership after his side collected 26 points in their first 17 league games that season. Louis van Gaal Period in charge: July 2014-May 2016 Number of games: 103 Win percentage: 52.4% Trophies: One Louis van Gaal took charge of Manchester United for two years until he was sacked days after winning the FA Cup and was replaced by Mourinho. Van Gaal oversaw a mixed period of results on the pitch - winning 54 games during his time in charge and earning a win rate of 52.4%. He had a 51.3% win percentage in the league (1.79 points per game) as Van Gaal achieved fourth and fifth place league finishes to add to the FA Cup win. David Moyes Period in charge: July 2013-April 2014 Number of games: 51 Win percentage: 52.9% Trophies: One David Moyes was handed the keys at Old Trafford after legendary boss Ferguson brought an end to his 26-year managerial stint at the club. Moyes was sacked after 10 months , winning 27 of the 51 games played in all competitions (52.9% win ratio). United won the 2013 Community Shield in his first game in charge, but he was sacked with the club in seventh with four matches left in the season. It was also the first time a United manager had been sacked since November 1986. Sir Alex Ferguson Manchester United won 38 trophies under Sir Alex Ferguson [Getty Images] Period in charge: November 1986-May 2013 Number of games: 1,503 Win percentage: 59.7% Trophies: 38 Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 after 26 years in charge of Manchester United. He guided the team to 897 wins and 338 draws in 1,503 games across all competitions. The Scotsman boasted an impressive 59.7% win rate - the highest of any permanent Manchester United boss. His win rate in the Premier League was even higher at 65.2%, earning an impressive 2.16 points per game. During his tenure, United won 13 league titles, two Champions Leagues, five FA Cups and four League Cups. This article is the latest from BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team. More questions answered... item.title: 🚨 Official: Pierre Sage sacked by Crystal Palace!
item.description: 🚨 Official: Pierre Sage sacked by Crystal Palace! The adventure was short-lived. Having joined Crystal Palace this summer after a historic season at RC Lens, Pierre Sage saw his English dream turn into a nightmare. On Thursday, the Eagles announced they had parted ways with the 47-year-old manager, less than three months into the season. Currently 20th in the Premier League, Crystal Palace are expected to appoint former Brentford and Tottenham manager Thomas Frank in the coming hours. Meanwhile, Pierre Sage could bounce back... at Lens! The former Lyon manager is among the favourites to replace Yannick Cahuzac, whose dismissal at Lens is expected to be officially announced in the coming hours. item.title: Trail Blazers Sweep Thunder in Statement Win That Ends Losing Streak
item.description: PORTLAND, OREGON - NOVEMBER 11: Deni Avdija #8 of the Portland Trail Blazers reacts after his dunk during the second half against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Moda Center on November 11, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty PORTLAND, OREGON - NOVEMBER 11: Deni Avdija #8 of the Portland Trail Blazers dives for a loose ball against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Moda Center on November 11, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Portland Trail Blazers did something against the Oklahoma City Thunder that had become increasingly difficult for them: they won twice in a row. Portland completed a two-game sweep with a 118-108 victory Wednesday night, following Tuesday’s 123-103 win. The back-to-back results ended a stretch in which the Blazers had lost 19 of their previous 20 meetings with Oklahoma City. For a Portland team still dealing with significant injuries, the turnaround was an encouraging sign. Trail Blazers Sweep Thunder After Two Very Different Tests Tuesday’s opener was largely about Portland taking control. Damian Lillard scored 25 points, including 13 in a decisive third quarter, while Deni Avdija added 24 points and eight assists. The Blazers outscored Oklahoma City 38-21 in the third and carried a 17-point advantage into the final period. Wednesday’s rematch demanded something different. Portland led by as many as 12 in the third quarter, but Oklahoma City fought back and briefly moved ahead 92-88 early in the fourth. Rather than let the game slip away, the Blazers responded with their best basketball when it mattered most. Avdija finished with 28 points, six assists and four steals, while Lillard added 18. Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko each scored 19 points, giving Portland the support it needed to close out the win. Avdija and Lillard combined for 20 of Portland’s 30 fourth-quarter points as the Blazers took control again. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty PORTLAND, OREGON - NOVEMBER 11: Deni Avdija #8 of the Portland Trail Blazers dives for a loose ball against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Moda Center on November 11, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Portland Trail Blazers did something against the Oklahoma City Thunder that had become increasingly difficult for them: they won twice in a row. Portland completed a two-game sweep with a 118-108 victory Wednesday night, following Tuesday’s 123-103 win. The back-to-back results ended a stretch in which the Blazers had lost 19 of their previous 20 meetings with Oklahoma City. For a Portland team still dealing with significant injuries, the turnaround was an encouraging sign. Trail Blazers Sweep Thunder After Two Very Different Tests Tuesday’s opener was largely about Portland taking control. Damian Lillard scored 25 points, including 13 in a decisive third quarter, while Deni Avdija added 24 points and eight assists. The Blazers outscored Oklahoma City 38-21 in the third and carried a 17-point advantage into the final period. Wednesday’s rematch demanded something different. Portland led by as many as 12 in the third quarter, but Oklahoma City fought back and briefly moved ahead 92-88 early in the fourth. Rather than let the game slip away, the Blazers responded with their best basketball when it mattered most. Avdija finished with 28 points, six assists and four steals, while Lillard added 18. Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko each scored 19 points, giving Portland the support it needed to close out the win. Avdija and Lillard combined for 20 of Portland’s 30 fourth-quarter points as the Blazers took control again. Getty PORTLAND, OREGON – NOVEMBER 11: Deni Avdija #8 of the Portland Trail Blazers dives for a loose ball against Shai Gilgeous-Alexander #2 of the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Moda Center on November 11, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Portland’s Depth Makes the Difference The two victories were particularly encouraging because Portland is not operating with a complete roster. Ja Morant remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, while Shaedon Sharpe and Vit Krejci have also been unavailable. The Blazers have had to make adjustments, including moving Scoot Henderson to the bench and giving Sidy Cissoko a larger role. Cissoko rewarded that decision with 17 points in Tuesday’s win before matching Holiday with 19 in the rematch. Holiday’s contribution was also important, particularly with his scoring coming off the bench Wednesday. Those performances show why Portland cannot rely exclusively on Lillard and Avdija to carry the offense every night. A Sweep That Means More Than Two Wins There is a reason these results stand out. Oklahoma City had won 19 of its previous 20 games against Portland, making the two victories a significant reversal of a recent pattern. The Thunder were also short-handed, with Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace among the key players unavailable. That context matters, but it does not erase what Portland accomplished. The Blazers showed they could win comfortably when their offense clicked and then respond when a game turned against them. They improved to 8-3, putting themselves in an excellent position early in the season despite the injuries and lineup changes. Two wins do not establish Portland as a Western Conference contender, and the team still has plenty to prove. But ending such a lopsided run against Oklahoma City while finding different ways to win on consecutive nights is meaningful progress. The Blazers are beginning to look like a team with enough depth and resilience to remain competitive even when circumstances are not ideal. item.title: NC State pulls away from Liberty, 71-47
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 08: Forward Khamil Pierre #12 of the NC State Wolfpack drives past center Clara Strack #13 of the Kentucky Wildcats during the first half of the 2026 Ally Tip Off at Spectrum Center on November 08, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the pall of Zoe Brooks’ injury lingering over the team, NC State pulled together without her and put together a dominant fourth quarter to down Liberty on Wednesday night. You would not guess it based on the final score, but Liberty was very much in this game, even into the last quarter. But Liberty also did not score a point over the last eight minutes, which is not a recommended way to finish a game. NC State did an excellent job on the offensive boards, led by Annsley Trivette, who had seven of those by herself, which helped the Pack’s somewhat listless offense. The defensive rebounding needs to be better and the effort in general was poor at times, but Liberty couldn’t find a hot hand in this one, and the Flames turned the ball over a bunch. It was an odd game in that both teams shot under 50% at the free throw line: Liberty was 1-6, State was 10-24. Not a pretty sight. Khamil Pierre led State with 19 points as the guards mostly struggled with Brooks out. Desiree Wooten played all 40 minutes but was just 3-10 from the field, and on a lot of nights, that’s going to be a tough stat line for the team to overcome. NC State returns to the floor against Seton Hall on Sunday.

item.title: Paralympic medalist Shuker ends 24-year tennis career
item.description: Lucy Shuker ends her career with a combined 139 singles and doubles titles [Getty Images] British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals. The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley. A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season. At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles. She was awarded the British Empire Medal for services to sport in 2023 and was GB's flagbearer for the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paralympics in Paris. "I would like to congratulate Lucy on her fantastic career and thank her for the contribution she has made to wheelchair tennis both on and off the court," said the LTA's chief executive Scott Lloyd. "To compete at the highest level of the game for over 20 years is a remarkable achievement and testament to her dedication and professionalism. "She has been, and will continue to be, a passionate advocate for the development of the sport and we look forward to working with her to continue to grow the game for future generations." Her last match came on Wednesday at the Wheelchair Tennis Finals in Barcelona, where she and Ksenia Chasteau were beaten 6-3 6-1 by the Dutch pair of Diede de Groot and Aniek Van Koot. Shuker spent most of her career ranked just outside the world's top 10 and ends her career ranked 23rd in the world, the British number two behind Cornelia Oosthuizen (20). item.title: Week 10 NFL Survivor strategy and picks
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars calls the snap against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is headed into the proverbial dog days before the holiday season heats up the playoff race. The trade deadline was this past Tuesday and it was plenty active. The Jaguars were the busiest team, while the Vikings made arguably the most important move, trading for Kirk Cousins after Carson Wentz stunk up the joint on Monday Night Football . If you were still alive in your Survivor pool headed into Week 9, you probably remain so heading into Week 10. There were very few upsets, with Packers over Patriots being the only betting upset. I took the Bears and it worked out for me, although the Bucs did give them some trouble. I’m back with my Week 10 Survivor picks ahead of Commanders-Giants on Thursday Night Football . Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. I’m down to one entry that has one strike against it, but I continue rolling along. Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend. I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel . Safest picks Jaguars (-10.5) over Titans Rams (-9.5) over Cardinals Bills (-8) over Jets These are the three favorites with a greater than touchdown spread. Early in the year it’s best to avoid divisional games, especially divisional road games. But now that we’re past the halfway point, you can’t necessarily be as picky. You’ll likely want to save some of these squads, but if your pool is getting light, these are all good picks. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and comments Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Best value picks Rams (-9.5) over Cardinals LA is going to be a popular pick this week for those who haven’t already used them. After this week, their biggest remaining odds are at home against the Packers in Week 12 and at home against the Cowboys in Week 15. Given how shaky the Rams have been, neither is a particularly compelling matchup. The Cardinals are down to their third string quarterback. item.content:encoded: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars calls the snap against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is headed into the proverbial dog days before the holiday season heats up the playoff race. The trade deadline was this past Tuesday and it was plenty active. The Jaguars were the busiest team, while the Vikings made arguably the most important move, trading for Kirk Cousins after Carson Wentz stunk up the joint on Monday Night Football . If you were still alive in your Survivor pool headed into Week 9, you probably remain so heading into Week 10. There were very few upsets, with Packers over Patriots being the only betting upset. I took the Bears and it worked out for me, although the Bucs did give them some trouble. I’m back with my Week 10 Survivor picks ahead of Commanders-Giants on Thursday Night Football . Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. I’m down to one entry that has one strike against it, but I continue rolling along. Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend. I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel . Safest picks Jaguars (-10.5) over Titans Rams (-9.5) over Cardinals Bills (-8) over Jets These are the three favorites with a greater than touchdown spread. Early in the year it’s best to avoid divisional games, especially divisional road games. But now that we’re past the halfway point, you can’t necessarily be as picky. You’ll likely want to save some of these squads, but if your pool is getting light, these are all good picks. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and comments Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Best value picks Rams (-9.5) over Cardinals LA is going to be a popular pick this week for those who haven’t already used them. After this week, their biggest remaining odds are at home against the Packers in Week 12 and at home against the Cowboys in Week 15. Given how shaky the Rams have been, neither is a particularly compelling matchup. The Cardinals are down to their third string quarterback. They might put up a fight, but they’re not winning this game. Trap pick Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins Texans (-5) over Browns The Seahawks are traveling to face a Raiders squad likely sending out rookie QB Fernando Mendoza. He’s a complete wild card in this game. Seattle’s defense probably creates too many problems for him, but I’d stay away from this game. The Colts have been dealing players left and right, but now we also have the Dolphins putting Malik Willis on injured reserve. Indy is tempting if you need to roll the dice, but stay away from it. Houston is a five point road favorite in Cleveland and is showing a bit more life of late. But the Browns are enough of a wild card team that you should stay away from this one. My picks this week I’ll be going with the Rams this week. I have the Jaguars and Bills available, but I’m saving them for upcoming weeks.

item.title: Why a salary cap matters so much
item.description: Dec 21, 2022; Bronx, New York, USA; Hal Steinbrenner during a press conference at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jessica Alcheh-USA TODAY Sports I remain, possibly foolishly, optimistic that the coming lockout won’t be as bad as some others say. Baseball’s having a bit of a hot streak, with the Dodgers playing the key role of central villain, young studs like Cam Schlittler and Jacob Misiorowski taking on the mantle of a baseball game’s protagonist, and we just saw in the World Series that it’s possible to win without just emptying your bank account to do so. Add to it that there’s this… general air of anger towards billionaires, toward the elite, that the likes of Steve Cohen and Hal Steinbrenner sneering about competitive balance will be less effective than I think they think it will be. Still, I’m a naturally cynical person, and I also understand how money works. Ownership is committed to a salary cap, and we know this because Hal himself has said so. CBA negotiations will go someway along the lines of the player’s union disregarding Item No. 1, a salary cap and floor, and ownership refusing to engage until the union agrees to negotiate on Item No. 1. Many have noted the irony that a cap/floor system would probably cost Bob Nutting or Bob Castellini or various other small-market Bobs more money on a year-to-year basis. A cap of $280 and floor of $120 (all moneys in millions of USD) would cost Nutting an additional $14 million based on his 2026 payroll allocation, meaning he’s forced to sign two relievers. But the key to a capped system is cost certainty, and what that certainty feeds. Year over year income is just less important than appreciation of the central asset, the franchise itself. Franchise valuation is the whole game here, as we’ve seen the Angels sell for four billion dollars, the Yankees agree to a $12ish billion valuation with Apollo, a private equity firm, and Mark Warner able to sell the LA Lakers at just about the same price. If certainty is the deadly enemy of tolerance, it is the great friend of the marketplace. Being able to project out three, five, ten years into the future what your payroll is going to be means your costs are relatively stable, while your income has upside in the form of new TV and streaming deals, as well as non-baseball revenue streams. This increases your franchise valuation, and critically, you’re able to borrow against that valuation to further invest — the Atlanta Braves and Washington Nationals, for example, are real estate developers that occasionally play baseball, and those valuations fund that development. That clubs are then able to write off the interest on those loans to lower their taxable income isn’t to be overlooked either. That’s my biggest fear, the biggest obstacle to a short lockout that leaves the season mostly untouched. item.content:encoded: Dec 21, 2022; Bronx, New York, USA; Hal Steinbrenner during a press conference at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jessica Alcheh-USA TODAY Sports I remain, possibly foolishly, optimistic that the coming lockout won’t be as bad as some others say. Baseball’s having a bit of a hot streak, with the Dodgers playing the key role of central villain, young studs like Cam Schlittler and Jacob Misiorowski taking on the mantle of a baseball game’s protagonist, and we just saw in the World Series that it’s possible to win without just emptying your bank account to do so. Add to it that there’s this… general air of anger towards billionaires, toward the elite, that the likes of Steve Cohen and Hal Steinbrenner sneering about competitive balance will be less effective than I think they think it will be. Still, I’m a naturally cynical person, and I also understand how money works. Ownership is committed to a salary cap, and we know this because Hal himself has said so. CBA negotiations will go someway along the lines of the player’s union disregarding Item No. 1, a salary cap and floor, and ownership refusing to engage until the union agrees to negotiate on Item No. 1. Many have noted the irony that a cap/floor system would probably cost Bob Nutting or Bob Castellini or various other small-market Bobs more money on a year-to-year basis. A cap of $280 and floor of $120 (all moneys in millions of USD) would cost Nutting an additional $14 million based on his 2026 payroll allocation, meaning he’s forced to sign two relievers. But the key to a capped system is cost certainty, and what that certainty feeds. Year over year income is just less important than appreciation of the central asset, the franchise itself. Franchise valuation is the whole game here, as we’ve seen the Angels sell for four billion dollars, the Yankees agree to a $12ish billion valuation with Apollo, a private equity firm, and Mark Warner able to sell the LA Lakers at just about the same price. If certainty is the deadly enemy of tolerance, it is the great friend of the marketplace. Being able to project out three, five, ten years into the future what your payroll is going to be means your costs are relatively stable, while your income has upside in the form of new TV and streaming deals, as well as non-baseball revenue streams. This increases your franchise valuation, and critically, you’re able to borrow against that valuation to further invest — the Atlanta Braves and Washington Nationals, for example, are real estate developers that occasionally play baseball, and those valuations fund that development. That clubs are then able to write off the interest on those loans to lower their taxable income isn’t to be overlooked either. That’s my biggest fear, the biggest obstacle to a short lockout that leaves the season mostly untouched. The owners can stomach some pain because of the windfall that will come if a cap controls their costs going forward. Even a cap negotiated to rise over time still presents that cost certainty, even a change to the arbitration system presents that cost certainty. I hope that the general cultural attitude toward the rich burns out any of the “millionaires playing a children’s game” rhetoric that ownership will rely on. I hope that the MLBPA strike fund is sufficient to hold over the younger players who haven’t signed their guaranteed deals yet. I’m worried that the perceived necessity of juicing franchise valuation will win out over all of that.

item.title: Manchester City Prepare New Contract for Highly-Rated Defender Amid Impressive Premier League Loan
item.description: Manchester City Prepare New Contract for Highly-Rated Defender Amid Impressive Premier League Loan Assessing Hugo Viana's start to life at Manchester City More Videos It can be hard for Manchester City supporters to keep tabs on the academy graduates out on loan every season, but when one gets off to a start like Stephen Mfuni at Coventry City , they are bound to catch the eye. The highly-rated teenage defender has not looked out of place since stepping up to the Premier League so far this season and is now securing regular starts to match under Frank Lampard. Having joined the Manchester City youth setup at under-9 level, the now-18 year-old, versatile defender has long been rated among the brightest prospects in East Manchester by officials around the club. After a season of gaining valuable Championship experience with Watford, Stephen Mfuni made a summer move to play under Lampard, and his solid start in the top-flight has prompted Manchester City to act over his long-term future. According to a new report by Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk , Manchester City are said to be 'delighted' with the progress Stephen Mfuni is making so far at the CBS Arena under Frank Lampard. Comfortable at both centre-back and left-back, the Wigan-born defender has nailed down a place in Lampard’s side, starting recent Premier League games against Sunderland and Everton. In fact, the report states that officials at Manchester City had initially considered keeping Stephen Mfuni in Enzo Maresca’s current squad this season, before ultimately deciding regular first-team football in the Premier League was the better next step for the player. That call is already paying off, with the teenager showing his versatility and composure against senior opposition on a regular basis. His displays will only have strengthened the club’s belief that Mfuni has the technical and physical tools to become a regular first-team option at the Etihad Stadium later on down the line. With his current deal entering its final months, Manchester City already hold the option to extend Stephen Mfuni’s stay, but the club would rather reward his progress with a completely fresh long-term agreement. They are reportedly keen to tie him down quickly before any rival suitors step up their interest, with the player's form having not gone unnoticed across the continent, with the likes of Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain said to be keeping tabs on his development. The German giants in particular, managed by former Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany, will be well aware of the talent coming through the academy in East Manchester through the Belgian's connections at the club. Despite that outside interest, City remain determined to keep hold of a defender they have nurtured for almost a decade, and as Stephen Mfuni adds to his senior experience, getting his signature on a new deal could prove to be a masterstroke for the club’s planning.

item.title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Steelers
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Pittsburgh Steelers in primetime football this week. They face off at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football with first place on the line in the division. Both teams enter this game at 6-2, with Pittsburgh taking a close win over Cincinnati in Week 3. Let’s look at some of the key matchups to watch in this massive AFC North clash. Amarius Mims vs. TJ Watt Amarius Mims has been playing at an All-Pro level all season long. Mims has allowed just five total pressures through eight regular-season games. He is absolutely locking guys down on his side of the line. He is also left on an island more than about any other tackle in the NFL. While he is starting to get more recognition, a primetime matchup for first place in the division against TJ Watt and the Pittsburgh Steelers could really boost his chances for an All-Pro this season. Meanwhile, TJ Watt has already surpassed his sack total from the 2025 season. Watt currently has 7.5 sacks through just eight games played. Last season, he recorded seven sacks during the entire season. Watt is still one of the better defenders in the league, but will certainly have his hands full trying to get around Mt. Mims this week. This is great versus great, and should be a must-see matchup. Amarius Mims has yet to allow a pressure through the first 3 games. He is the only starting tackle in the league to have done so. Mims is Hims. pic.twitter.com/3LzW9PVusO — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 29, 2026 Darnell Washington vs. Jordan Battle Tackling Darnell Washington is not a fun task, and the Bengals have been one of the worst teams at trying to do so over the years. Washington had 67 yards against the Bengals during Week 3, including a big rumble down the sideline during the 4th quarter. There was also a play earlier in the game where Jordan Battle tried to come in high on Washington and make the tackle. It won’t be just Battle who has to play well against Washington, but it would be nice to see him learn from his mistakes against him earlier in the season. As for Jordan Battle, it feels like he has started to play some pretty solid football the past few games. His tackling overall has been much more sound, and he made some huge plays against Tennessee in coverage a couple of weeks ago. This past game against Atlanta was the first game of the season that he was not credited with a single missed tackle. Hopefully that is a positive sign for this week, because Washington is a BIG test. Regardless of the angle you see it from, a lot of pathetic effort out there to go and make this play after the Darnell Washington catch. pic.twitter.com/9HKBpp1YMo — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Jaylen Warren vs. Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. Jaylen Warren was incredible in Week 3 against the Bengals, who had a hard time getting him on the ground all day long. Warren had 17 carries for 117 yards rushing. He also added an additional three receptions for another 49 yards. The Bengals will have to keep Warren in check if they want to get the win this week. Two of the main guys responsible for making sure he doesn’t have another game like that will be Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter. Not how you want to start the game pic.twitter.com/SdCNgOqiVe — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 If the Bengals are going to continue having Barrett Carter out there 100% of the snaps (and they likely are) we are going to need him to play better. pic.twitter.com/ao1dBAcJh1 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Chase Brown vs. Pittsburgh Defense The Bengals are always going to be a pass-first team, but that doesn’t mean that Chase Brown cannot have some big rushing performances. item.title: Wilkes Weekly: Pens take two in Charlotte
item.description: CLEVELAND, OH - OCTOBER 16: Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins defenseman Jake Livanavage (4) defends Cleveland Monsters left wing Luke Tuch (17) during the third period of the American Hockey League game between the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins and Cleveland Monsters on October 16, 2026, at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, OH. (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins had a successful last weekend, going to first-place Charlotte and winning two games on the road. Here’s WBSPenguins.com recap of the week: Friday, Nov. 6 – PENGUINS 4 at Charlotte 3 (OT) Down 3-0 past the mid-point of the third period, Wilkes-Barre/ Scranton stormed back with four unanswered goals to shock the Checkers. Daniel Russell, Rafaël Harvey-Pinard and Rutger McGroarty all scored in under four minutes to pull the Penguins even. After a successful penalty kill in OT, Jake Livanavage completed the comeback with the extra-time winner. Saturday, Nov. 7 – PENGUINS 4 at Charlotte 1 Once again, the Penguins toppled the division-leading Checkers with four-straight goals. Ryan Johnson’s first goal in Black and Gold started the surge in the second period, swiftly followed by strikes from Finn Harding and Avery Hayes. Hugh McGing rounded out the offense with a scorching release in the third. That winning roll would grind to a halt. In the rare AHL mid-week game, WBS lost 4-0 at home to Utica on Tuesday night. Utica has now won five straight games and just had too much going for them according to head coach Kirk MacDonald who had to admit his team just wasn’t the better side on that night. "I would argue this is the first loss where I'm not sitting here (saying) we gave two points away. " Sometimes you just have to tip your cap to other team, and that's what #WBSPens HC Kirk MacDonald did after last night's loss to Utica 📽 @InsideAHLHockey … — Tony Androckitis* (@TonyAndrock) November 11, 2026 The busy times continue coming up with three games in three days over the weekend. WBS will be in Hershey tomorrow night before returning home to play Hamilton on Saturday. Then on Sunday the Pens host Lehigh Valley for the first of 12 (count ‘em, 12!) meetings this season against a cross-state and division rival. The game to circle back and focus on was last Friday’s big comeback against Charlotte. WBS was down 3-0 before mounting a furious comeback. Rutger McGroarty scored the tying goal and then Jake Livanavage, freshly back from a stint of NHL healthy scratches, notched the overtime winner. LIVER CALLS GAME pic.twitter.com/zqhtO54QTz — Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins (@WBSPenguins) November 7, 2026 Here was the lineup on that night. Jake Livanavage rejoins us in Charlotte Don’t miss a second of the action by tuning in on the radio or on AHLTV on FloHockey: 📻 https://t.co/8q6455YWWg 📺 https://t.co/oFOWvR0WAh pic.twitter.com/RhSgHUXP4y — Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins (@WBSPenguins) November 6, 2026 The lineup, as alway

" Sometimes you just have to tip your cap to other team, and that's what #WBSPens HC Kirk MacDonald did after last night's loss to Utica 📽 @InsideAHLHockey … — Tony Androckitis* (@TonyAndrock) November 11, 2026 The busy times continue coming up with three games in three days over the weekend. WBS will be in Hershey tomorrow night before returning home to play Hamilton on Saturday. The game to circle back and focus on was last Friday’s big comeback against Charlotte. WBS was down 3-0 before mounting a furious comeback. Rutger McGroarty scored the tying goal and then Jake Livanavage, freshly back from a stint of NHL healthy scratches, notched the overtime winner. LIVER CALLS GAME pic.twitter.com/zqhtO54QTz — Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins (@WBSPenguins) November 7, 2026 Here was the lineup on that night. Jake Livanavage rejoins us in Charlotte Don’t miss a second of the action by tuning in on the radio or on AHLTV on FloHockey: 📻 https://t.co/8q6455YWWg 📺 https://t.co/oFOWvR0WAh pic.twitter.com/RhSgHUXP4y — Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins (@WBSPenguins) November 6, 2026 The lineup, as always is the case at any level but especially in the AHL, has been fluctuating. Owen Pickering got injured during the Saturday night game and missed the Utica match on Tuesday, but it’s believed his injury is somewhat minor. Harrison Brunicke missed both the weekend games with the injury he suffered in the end of October but was able to return for Tuesday night’s game. As mentioned above, Livanavage has bounced back and forth from the NHL, as has McGroarty. For recent goaltender outcomes, Taylor Gauthier picked up the Friday night win in the comeback game, stopping 29/32 shots. Joel Blomqvist played the other two games, having one of his best games to only allow one goal on 18 shots in the Saturday win over Charlotte. Blomqvist also played in the overmatched game against Utica, stopping 32 of 35 shots before an empty net goal was chipped in. Wilkes sits fourth in the standings for total points, though they’re third in points percentage since Hartford has played four more games than the Penguins to this point. The division looks like it’s starting to separate between a top 3-4 teams (Charlotte, Hershey, WBS and maybe Hartford) before dropping away to a bottom three teams with under a .500 points% (Providence, Lehigh Valley, Springfield). The good news for the Pens is they’re scoring more than most and allowing fewer goals on the season, take out those pesky pair of losses to Utica and WBS’s place would be even better. Teams that do well against the division are usually going to be alright by the end of the season, making the upcoming weekend games against Hershey and LV very critical in the big scheme of things. The top six teams in the division make the playoffs in the unorthodox AHL playoff setup, so the Pens should be in really good shape for clearing the low bar of at least making the postseason. As usual, their goal should be trying to finish in the top-two of their division and avoid the opening round best-of-three quick playoff series where a bad couple of days could bring the curtain down on their season. For now, the playoffs are a long way off and the grind of the minor league season will be in full view with the dreaded three-in-three weekend.

item.title: Barring late injury or illness, Wael Mohya won’t dress for Germany vs. Serbia
item.description: (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) | Getty Images for DFB Jürgen Klopp has made his first difficult selection decision ahead of Germany’s clash with Serbia tomorrow, with Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster Wael Mohya set to miss out on the matchday squad. According to Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Klopp nominated 24 players for the fixture, but only 23 can be included in the official matchday squad. That means one player had to be sacrificed, and the decision has fallen on the 17-year-old, who is rumored to be on the radar of several clubs, including Bayern Munich. item.title: Dave Portnoy responds to people calling for The Duke to be banned from next year’s Internet Invitational
item.description: Photo by Theo Wargo/Getty Images The Internet Invitational has taken over the golfing world. Millions are tuning in to each episode to watch amateur golfers compete for $1.3 million. The field consists of players of all abilities, from high-handicap hackers to former PGA Tour pros. The barrier to entry for this event isn’t talent, it’s entertainment, with some of the best moments of the tournament so far coming from the worst golfers delivering their worst golf. But one player in particular, who goes by The Duke, performed so badly at this year’s Internet Invitational that fans called for him to never be invited back. Dave Portnoy responds to calls for The Duke to be banned from the Internet Invitational The Duke caused a stir at the Internet Invitational when he made it all the way to the penultimate round. He was put on a team with Ryan Ruffles, who had been the tournament’s best player up to that point, and Marissa Wenzler. In many fans’ eyes, that team’s fate was sealed the moment The Duke was put on it, and they finished dead last that round, sending all three players home. Many believed that he simply isn’t good enough to be in the tournament, and it ruins any player’s chances of winning if he is put on their team. Portnoy, however, believed The Duke didn’t play up to his albeit low standard. He said, “People say it should be Duke’s last Invitational. Let me tell you something. The Duke played so bad, and I’m not even saying he’s bad, we know that, but I mean bad for The Duke. Because he was f—–g nervous. “I think for the first time in the tournament, he’s smelling $1.3 million, which changes his life. He’d probably be dead to be honest. If The Duke won $1.3 million he’s probably dead, he wouldn’t be able to take it. “But I think he was smelling it and he got f—–g nervous. He was almost like a much different guy to a degree, and the pressure go to him which is the point of the tournament. “And he said, I don’t know if it was on camera I didn’t watch all of it because obviously I know everything that happens. But it’s like, ‘I get if you don’t invite me back. I get it. I had my chance, I totally get it if I’m not coming back next year.’ “So we’ll see. I don’t think a decision has been made on that either way. I think I’ve input enough where if I said, ‘we absolutely can’t have this guy any more’, I think Bob and Fore Play would value that. “But for the billionth time, I don’t make the list. I don’t invite people. I don’t pick them out, I don’t disinvite. Not me.” Admittedly, Ruffles and Wenzler also didn’t play their best golf either, as the nerves got to all three players. It seems harsh to put it all on The Duke, who was one of many high-handicappers at the event.
