item.title: ‘Hard to find minutes’ – Mike Brown delivers brutal message to Knicks’ struggling $150 million star
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown has shared his blunt take on the future of the team’s rotation amid one of his starters being stuck in the worst stretch of his career. The Knicks have rebounded from their 0-3 start to the season by going 6-2 over the last eight games to re-establish themselves as one of the clear-cut playoff contenders in the NBA. However, one of the reasons for New York’s struggles relates to one of their key forwards no longer looking like the star he was when the team acquired him and extended him on a four-year, $150 million contract. Knicks coach Mike Brown admits Mikal Bridges will be losing his minutes The player in question is former Defensive Player of the Year runner-up Mikal Bridges, who has averaged 5.9 points on 24.4 minutes per game so far this season. As he continues losing minutes to role players, coach Brown confirmed that he cannot afford to suppress the likes of Landry Shamet and Deuce McBride by forcing Bridges into minutes where he’s clearly struggling to perform. “We got two guys who are playing really well in Landry and Deuce. So it’s gonna be hard to find minutes at times for Mikal.” The Knicks sent the Brooklyn Nets the equivalent of six first-round picks a few seasons ago to acquire Bridges after the development he showed offensively while remaining one of the best perimeter defenders in the NBA. Now, Bridges is performing worse than the average role player in the NBA, while his defence has not been good enough to justify his minutes. He looks like a shadow of the player he was last season. With Bridges losing minutes, real questions can be asked about his future, as the penny-pinching Knicks would be better off parting with the $150 million they owe Mikal over four years and ensuring they open up the room to extend Josh Hart, McBride, and Karl-Anthony Towns. This is an inexplicable regression that both Bridges and the Knicks will hope can be addressed soon, as the franchise needs his high-motor perimeter presence and scoring threat to be the championship-winning squad we know them to be. item.title: Rice vs. Tulane: How to watch, date, time, TV channel
item.description: Will Swartz and Rice return home for an American conference game against Tulane on Saturday. (Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Rice returns home this weekend once again looking to end its long losing streak. The Owls (1-8, 0-5 American) have dropped eight consecutive games since beating Houston Christian in their season opener. Three of those defeats have been at home, two by one-score margins. Tulane (4-5, 2-3), meanwhile, is licking its wounds after being beat 60-10 by Tulsa in the Green Wave's homecoming game last week. The teams' head-to-head series dates to 1916, with Rice leading 20-17-1. The Green Wave have won each of the past two years in conference games. Rice vs. Tulane When: 1 p.m. Saturday Where: First Community Stadium TV: ESPN+ with David Saltzman (play-by-play), Marcus "Doc" Holliday (analyst) and Smacker Danielson (sideline reporter). Radio: Varsity Network app/RiceOwls.com with JP Heath, Nate Griffin and Luke Mauro 2026 Rice football schedule Sept. 5: beat Houston Christian, 31-3 Sept. 12: lost to No. 3 Notre Dame, 52-0 Sept. 19: lost to Western Michigan, 28-21 Sept. 26: lost to Fresno State, 38-24 Oct. 3: lost to UTSA, 16-14 Oct. 10: lost to East Carolina, 28-12 Oct. 17: lost to Tulsa, 38-17 Oct. 24: lost to Florida Atlantic, 51-49 Nov. 7: lost to North Texas, 52-23 Nov. 14: vs. Tulane, 1 p.m. (ESPN+) Nov. 19: at Temple, 6:30 p.m. (ESPN) Nov. 28: vs. Army, time and TV TBD Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: Red Sox Veteran Targets Return After Dominant Stretch
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - APRIL 22: Darwinzon Hernandez #63 of the Boston Red Sox looks on after allowing four runs during the tenth inning against the Seattle Mariners cat Fenway Park on April 22, 2021 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty Images The Boston Red Sox could have an interesting opportunity to revisit a familiar name as they continue evaluating their pitching options for the 2027 season. The organization has several decisions to make this offseason, particularly when it comes to building a bullpen capable of supporting its rotation. While Boston will have plenty of established free agents and trade candidates to consider, the international market could also offer some intriguing possibilities. One former Red Sox pitcher has spent the past several seasons rebuilding his career overseas after struggling to establish himself in the major leagues. His departure from Boston came after command issues undermined some otherwise impressive strikeout numbers, leaving questions about whether his raw stuff would ever translate into consistent big-league success. Now, however, the 29-year-old left-hander is looking for another opportunity in MLB after putting together an impressive stretch in Japan. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Red Sox Issue Sonny Gray Statement After Team Exit Former Boston Red Sox Pitcher Eyes MLB Return According to Boston Globe reporter Alex Speier, Darwinzon Hernandez is interested in returning to the majors after spending the last four seasons with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks. “Left-hander Darwinzon Hernandez, who improved his control and has excelled in NPB over the last four years (2.46 ERA, 31 percent strikeout rate, 8 percent walk rate), is looking to return to MLB. He turns 30 in December,” Speier reported . Hernandez originally reached the majors with Boston in 2019 after developing within the organization’s farm system. He spent parts of four seasons with the Red Sox, appearing in 91 games and recording an uneven 5.06 ERA across 85 1/3 innings. The left-hander always possessed considerable strikeout ability, fanning 32.3% of opposing hitters during his major-league tenure. However, his 17.7% walk rate proved difficult to overcome. Boston designated him for assignment in January 2023 before he eventually landed with the Baltimore Orioles. After being released that July, he signed with the SoftBank Hawks. His subsequent performance in Japan suggests he has made meaningful progress. Hernandez has maintained his ability to miss bats while substantially reducing the number of hitters he allows to reach base through walks. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty Images The Boston Red Sox could have an interesting opportunity to revisit a familiar name as they continue evaluating their pitching options for the 2027 season. Now, however, the 29-year-old left-hander is looking for another opportunity in MLB after putting together an impressive stretch in Japan. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Red Sox Issue Sonny Gray Statement After Team Exit Former Boston Red Sox Pitcher Eyes MLB Return According to Boston Globe reporter Alex Speier, Darwinzon Hernandez is interested in returning to the majors after spending the last four seasons with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks. “Left-hander Darwinzon Hernandez, who improved his control and has excelled in NPB over the last four years (2.46 ERA, 31 percent strikeout rate, 8 percent walk rate), is looking to return to MLB. He turns 30 in December,” Speier reported . Hernandez originally reached the majors with Boston in 2019 after developing within the organization’s farm system. He spent parts of four seasons with the Red Sox, appearing in 91 games and recording an uneven 5.06 ERA across 85 1/3 innings. The left-hander always possessed considerable strikeout ability, fanning 32.3% of opposing hitters during his major-league tenure. However, his 17.7% walk rate proved difficult to overcome. Boston designated him for assignment in January 2023 before he eventually landed with the Baltimore Orioles. After being released that July, he signed with the SoftBank Hawks. His subsequent performance in Japan suggests he has made meaningful progress. Hernandez has maintained his ability to miss bats while substantially reducing the number of hitters he allows to reach base through walks. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Phillies Acquire New Backstop After JT Realmuto Decision Boston Red Sox Veteran Could Offer MLB Teams Low-Cost Option There are still reasons for potential suitors to exercise caution. Nippon Professional Baseball can be a more pitcher-friendly environment than MLB, and improved command overseas does not necessarily guarantee the same results against major-league hitters. Nevertheless, Hernandez could become an intriguing alternative for teams that miss out on more established left-handed relievers. “The lefty relief market is highlighted by Adrián Morejón but also features Alex Vesia, Steven Okert, JoJo Romero and plenty of others,” Darragh McDonald noted for MLB Trade Rumors . “For teams who miss out on those options, they could perhaps look to Hernández as a low-cost alternative.” For Boston, a reunion could offer an opportunity to evaluate how much Hernandez has changed since his previous stint with the organization. Whether the Red Sox pursue that possibility or another MLB club takes a chance on the left-hander, his success overseas has given him a new opportunity to get back to the majors. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Dianna Russini explains how her husband gave her ‘perspective’ after Mike Vrabel scandal
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Dianna Russini made her official return on Wednesday evening following a number of months trying to stay out of the limelight after her offseason controversies. The former reporter for The Athletic is making an attempt to make it on her own after leaving the sports outlet after her relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was made public during the offseason. Although she has been out of work for a number of months, Russini’s return has not come without criticism. The 43-year-old’s new show has been hit with scrutiny as she chose to address her controversies with Vrabel in a jovial manner. Dianna Russini brings her husband into Mike Vrabel controversy upon media return Following her return on Wednesday, Russini took to social media to thank everyone for helping her break an audience record with her new show. Although the views may have been there, some of her comments about her situation have left a bitter taste in the mouths of her viewers. “But first, a personal note.Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life, my priorities, and the person I want to be moving forward. Being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys, and being truly present, gave me so much perspective that I didn’t even know I needed,” she said. “I’ve also had a lot of long conversations with people all around football: some were about the game, and others were just about life. To the people who picked up the phone, checked in, and offered both encouragement and honest advice, from the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Russini has been spotted out in public with her husband since the situation involving her and Vrabel was revealed. Adam Schefter admitted he would still promote Russini’s work , if he was able to verify it, in what will be a boost for her going forward. There will be a long road back for Russini if she is to be taken seriously in the world an NFL insider, but the league has shown over the years that second chances are often provided to those who look to make up for their wrongdoing. item.title: JJ Redick Provides Updates on Doncic, Reaves and Sexton Injuries, Mamukelashvili Could Have Bigger Offensive Role
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) falls to the floor after injuring his ankle in the fourth quarter against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor Although the Los Angeles Lakers left the court with a seventh straight victory Wednesday night in Milwaukee, it certainly came at a cost after injuries to three of their top contributors. Entering Wednesday’s game flying high after back-to-back wins in Detroit and Atlanta to begin their road trip, the Lakers had little trouble keeping the winning streak going en route to a 123-112 win. The Lakers (11-2) welcomed back guard Austin Reaves after he missed the previous game due to an illness. But after seeing Reaves exit the game in the third quarter due to a heel injury , Lakers coach JJ Redick said the team will need to undergo further imaging and testing before knowing the severity of the injury to their No. 2 scoring option. In addition to Reaves’ injury, the team saw reserve guard Collin Sexton exit the game with a facial laceration after an inadvertent headbutt by Bucks guard Ryan Rollins . Another injury scare came later, when Lakers superstar Luka Doncic tweaked his right ankle after coming down on Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma ‘s foot following a jumper. And while Redick says Doncic’s injury isn’t believed to be serious, the team will know more about Reaves’s injury on Thursday. “X-rays were negative,” Redick said while giving an update on the Reaves injury. “We’ll get imaging tomorrow. Probably no update besides that. Luka, I think, is fine—just a light tweak. And then, obviously, Collin is getting sutures in his temple or whatever area he got hit. But no update on AR until we have imaging tomorrow.” JJ Redick says Austin Reaves’ X-rays were negative, with additional imaging scheduled for tomorrow. https://t.co/4jyKiJdZbn — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 12, 2026 Reaves and Doncic Were Playing Well Before Their Respective Injuries Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick talks with guard Austin Reaves (15) and guard Luka Doncic (77) during the fourth quarter against the Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum. Photo Credit: Petre Thomas, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Before exiting the game in the third quarter, Reaves scored 18 points on 6-of-10 shooting in 25 minutes. He also grabbed three rebounds, dished five assists and collected three steals before appearing to suffer the injury on a dunk attempt. Now, the team awaits news on the extent of the injury, although Redick said it’s not believed to be an Achilles injury . JJ Redick told reporters that the Lakers have ruled out an Achilles injury for Austin Reaves. — Jovan Buha (@jovanbuha) November 12, 2026 Meanwhile, Doncic told reporters after the game that he’s “good,” and was more focused on the team moving to 3-0 on their current road trip. Doncic scored 32 points on 10-of-25 shooting and 5-for-12 from three-point range in the win, adding five rebounds, five assists and two steal

Photo Credit: Petre Thomas, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Before exiting the game in the third quarter, Reaves scored 18 points on 6-of-10 shooting in 25 minutes. He also grabbed three rebounds, dished five assists and collected three steals before appearing to suffer the injury on a dunk attempt. Now, the team awaits news on the extent of the injury, although Redick said it’s not believed to be an Achilles injury . JJ Redick told reporters that the Lakers have ruled out an Achilles injury for Austin Reaves. — Jovan Buha (@jovanbuha) November 12, 2026 Meanwhile, Doncic told reporters after the game that he’s “good,” and was more focused on the team moving to 3-0 on their current road trip. Doncic scored 32 points on 10-of-25 shooting and 5-for-12 from three-point range in the win, adding five rebounds, five assists and two steals. Doncic subbed out of the game with the final score no longer in doubt. And according to Doncic, he’ll be “fine” when the team returns to action on Sunday in Phoenix. “I’m good,” Doncic said . “Obviously, it’s painful a little bit, but I’ll be fine. We got to 3-0 on this road trip, so that’s very good.” Sandro Mamukelashvili Has Stepped Up in Two Straight Games Should the Lakers be without Reaves for a period, Sandro Mamukelashvili has shown he’s ready to assume more offensive responsibility if needed. Mamukelashvili scored 23 points off the bench in Monday night’s win in Atlanta. He followed it up with a second straight game of 23 points in 26 minutes off the bench Wednesday night, registering three rebounds, two assists and a steal in the win. Mamukelashvili connected on 9-of-15 shooting from the field and 5-for-8 from three-point range on Wednesday. And if Reaves is forced to miss time, Mamukelashvili could emerge as a key contributor for the Lakers on offense. Mamu opens up about rebuilding his confidence and finding the freedom to be himself with the #Lakers. 💜💛 https://t.co/jxbNiXHowr — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 12, 2026 The Last Word Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams (11) dunks in the third quarter against the Milwaukee Bucks at Fiserv Forum. Photo Credit: Benny Sieu, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect In addition to the three players who suffered injuries, the Lakers were without Quentin Grimes for a second straight contest due to a finger injury. Grimes’ injury is a little concerning only because he was listed as questionable prior to being ruled out. Meanwhile, it seems that Redick is mainly concerned about Reeves heel injury. Heel injuries can be tricky, though most NBA players are back within a couple of days to a week, per Hashtag Basketball . But, depending on severity and the actual type of injury, Reeves could be out for up to a month. The good news is that the Lakers are off until Sunday when they close out their four-game road trip at Phoenix. If Reeves does miss time, Ziaire Williams figures to move back into the starting lineup, though Redick could go with Grimes. Williams has started five games, including the lone game that Reeves sat out, with the Lakers winning four of them. The 25-year-old has been highly effective whether coming off the bench or starting. Conversely, Grimes has been much more productive in his two starts than coming off the bench. But he has not been as efficient at shooting the ball in those two contests as he was the rest of the season. item.title: 'Another depressing moment' - Manchester United Supporters’ Trust slams ownership after Michael Carrick sacking
item.description: Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick following a disastrous start to the Premier League season. However, the club's prominent supporters' trust has swiftly shifted the blame towards the ownership, demanding immediate accountability for the ongoing crisis at Old Trafford. Carrick sacked after dismal Premier League start United have dismissed Carrick just ten matches into the new Premier League campaign. The club currently sit inside the relegation zone after securing a solitary domestic victory. Club executives met with minority owner Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to decide the manager's fate. A subsequent official statement confirmed the extremely difficult decision to make a change in pursuit of their ambitions. Despite his rapid exit, the Red Devils paid tribute to the former midfielder as a club legend. However, his departure has immediately sparked fierce backlash from the fanbase regarding the wider structure at Old Trafford. Supporters trust direct anger at club ownership The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST) quickly responded to the sacking, describing the decision as another depressing moment for the club. They argued that the fundamental problems lie squarely with the hierarchy rather than the dugout. "Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United," a MUST statement read. "We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished. "The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager. "They lie with the ownership. The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but." Deepening divisions and frustration at Old Trafford Frustration has been building both in the stands and on the pitch in recent weeks. Defender Lisandro Martinez notably criticised the hierarchy for failing to support Carrick in the transfer market following their recent Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid . MUST also highlighted a deeper deterioration at the club, pointing to unprecedented booing and aggressive ticketing policies. They claimed supporters are being forced to pay the price for ongoing boardroom mismanagement. "It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability," MUST stated. "But the discontent at United is not just about matters on the pitch. Far from it. "Aggressive ticketing policies have further damaged relations with supporters. item.content:encoded: Manchester United v AFC Bournemouth - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick following a disastrous start to the Premier League season. However, the club's prominent supporters' trust has swiftly shifted the blame towards the ownership, demanding immediate accountability for the ongoing crisis at Old Trafford. Carrick sacked after dismal Premier League start United have dismissed Carrick just ten matches into the new Premier League campaign. The club currently sit inside the relegation zone after securing a solitary domestic victory. Club executives met with minority owner Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to decide the manager's fate. A subsequent official statement confirmed the extremely difficult decision to make a change in pursuit of their ambitions. Despite his rapid exit, the Red Devils paid tribute to the former midfielder as a club legend. However, his departure has immediately sparked fierce backlash from the fanbase regarding the wider structure at Old Trafford. Supporters trust direct anger at club ownership The Manchester United Supporters’ Trust (MUST) quickly responded to the sacking, describing the decision as another depressing moment for the club. They argued that the fundamental problems lie squarely with the hierarchy rather than the dugout. "Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United," a MUST statement read. "We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished. "The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager. "They lie with the ownership. The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but." Deepening divisions and frustration at Old Trafford Frustration has been building both in the stands and on the pitch in recent weeks. Defender Lisandro Martinez notably criticised the hierarchy for failing to support Carrick in the transfer market following their recent Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid . MUST also highlighted a deeper deterioration at the club, pointing to unprecedented booing and aggressive ticketing policies. They claimed supporters are being forced to pay the price for ongoing boardroom mismanagement. "It is time for the owners to explain themselves and show some accountability," MUST stated. "But the discontent at United is not just about matters on the pitch. Far from it. "Aggressive ticketing policies have further damaged relations with supporters. Treating loyal fans principally as a source of revenue undermines their identity and the bond with the team that sustains support through difficult times. Supporters are being asked to pay the price for the owners’ mismanagement as well as their stadium ambitions through higher charges and diminished rights." Pochettino lined up as next manager The United board must now move swiftly to appoint a capable successor. Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino , who currently manages the United States men's national team, is firmly in line to take the reins. The incoming manager will inherit a divided club and a squad desperate for immediate results to escape the relegation zone.

item.title: Pierre Sage sacked by Crystal Palace after 16 games with club bottom of league
item.description: Thomas Frank the leading contender to take over Palace have conceded league-high 24 goals Pierre Sage has been sacked as Crystal Palace’s manager after 16 games. The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has gone after Sunday’s 3-1 defeat by Liverpool left his team bottom of the Premier League. Thomas Frank, out of work since his dismissal by Spurs in February, has emerged as the main candidate to succeed Sage. He spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford. Continue reading...

item.title: FPL: Which Leeds United players have impressed so far?
item.description: FPL: Which Leeds United players have impressed so far? Leeds have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Leeds United have made an encouraging start to the 2026/27 Premier League season and, as such, so have our players in FPL. All the regular starters in Daniel Farke’s side are on track to better their FPL points returns from last season over the course of the current campaign. Here we assess the underlying data and what that means for investing in Leeds players over the coming weeks. Leading the line: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m) has had 19 shots so far this season. Of those, 17 have come from inside the box, 10 have been on target and eight have been defined as OPTA big chances. The England international is ranked in the top 10 forwards in the game for all of these metrics. Meanwhile, Anton Stach (£6.0m), Ethan Ampadu (£5.3m) and Jayden Bogle (£4.8m) have all created a team-leading 10 chances this season. Stach has started seven encounters while Ampadu and Bogle have been deployed from the off in every game so far. Summer signing Harry Wilson (£6.1m) has also created an impressive nine chances across his three starts and five appearances from the bench. Calvert-Lewin is top for expected goal involvements (xGI) across the Leeds side with a xGI of 4.76. This is sixth across all the forwards in the game. Bogle and Tarik Muharemović (£5.1m) are also posting some excellent attacking numbers, with Bogle third of all the defenders in the game for xGI. Muharemović has had seven shots this season, all from inside the box. A strong defence: However, it is not just Muharemović’s attacking numbers that make him one of the best defender picks in the game. The Bosnian has registered 14 Defensive Contribution points this season, the most of any player in the game. He has completed 112 defensive actions across the opening 10 weeks of the season, which only one player in the game can better. Seven members of the Whites’ squad have recorded Defensive Contribution points this season. Of the backline, Nico Elvedi (£4.5m) and James Justin (£4.5m) have registered six with Jaka Bijol (£5.0m) collecting four. The Leeds defence has kept four clean sheets so far this season. Only two teams in Premier League can better that tally. We have also conceded the sixth-fewest big chances in the top-flight and the fifth-fewest shots from inside the box. With strong defensive underlying data, investing in a Leeds defender in FPL could be a very sensible decision. England international James Trafford (£5.0m) is having a fantastic season since his club-record signing in the summer. item.title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
item.description: Arvid Lindblad (left) and Liam Lawson have taken Racing Bulls to fifth place in the constructors' championship on 114 points, 45 points ahead of Alpine [Getty Images] Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027. Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up. Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing." The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme. Chequered Flag Extra: The Making of Kimi Antonelli Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded. That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled. The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist. Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season. The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points. Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving. "It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship. "I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together." Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support. "I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season." The news release announcing the pairing made no mention of Tsolov, who is expected to be retained by Red Bull in some form of reserve role in which he gains experience through work in the simulator and with testing previous cars. No. 6 Texas visits No. 21 LSU with edge rusher Colin Simmons and receiver Cam Coleman off the injury report, and the total is the better bet in a meeting of two top-five defenses. item.title: ‘Pretty rough’… Bill Simmons calls out ‘weird’ NFL trade that reminded him of Mat Ishbia on the Phoenix Suns
item.description: Photo by Rebecca Sapp/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Podcaster Bill Simmons has called out the Jacksonville Jaguars for what he views as a risky all-in move at the NFL trade deadline. The Jacksonville Jaguars’ 6-2 start to the season has the team believing they can make a Super Bowl run. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence even received MVP chants during their recent win in Baltimore. The Jaguars were among the more aggressive movers at the trade deadline, giving up a 2027 first round pick and 2029 second round pick to acquire Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles. The move for the defensive tackle came after trades for Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, and followed injuries to DaVon Hamilton and Eric Murray. Speaking to his podcast , Bill Simmons called out the Jaguars for overpaying for Jordan Davis. He also compared the dealings to the moves made by the owner of NBA team the Phoenix Suns, Mat Ishbia. Ishbia went ‘all-in’ with the team when he traded for Kevin Durant and Bradley Beal to add around Devin Booker, but the move was not a success. Simmons explained: “The weird one was Jacksonville, Jordan Davis. They gave up extra picks, including a first for Travis Hunter [previously]. They now gave up a first for Jordan Davis. “This general manager, James Gladstone, he’s basically doing the Matt Ishbia, ‘I’m going to set all my picks on fire and try to win this season move’, which I’m not a big fan of. “The Jordan Davis thing was especially weird because nobody seemed to think he was playing that well. He was only playing half the snaps “I couldn’t believe how much they gave up for him. So Jacksonville is all in and they feel like rightly so that they have a chance to win the AFC, but I’m not sure Jordan Davis was the answer. “If you had asked me Jacksonville is traded for Jordan Davis, what do you think they gave up? I would have said a second because that would have been end of the second round because they’re going to have a good record. It was a first and a second. It’s pretty rough.” Jaguars have strong chance to win next three The Jaguars are already clear at 6-2 in the AFC South, followed by the trailing 3-5 Houston Texans. Liam Coen’s team could soon be out of sight. In the next three games they face the 1-7 Tennessee Titans, a 5-2-1 New York Giants team struggling at quarterback, and then the Titans again. They then face a possible Super Bowl matchup when they visit the Chicago Bears on the road, which will be a real test. item.title: Ancelotti keeps Brazil's system with a 'makeshift' forward
item.description: Ancelotti keeps Brazil's system with a 'makeshift' forward For the first time since arriving in Singapore, coach Carlo Ancelotti had his full squad on the pitch on Thursday and tried out changes to Brazil's starting lineup. According to ge, the Italian coach retained the 4-3-3 formation used in the previous two friendlies and tested Bournemouth forward Rayan in a deeper midfield role just behind Raphinha. Also according to ge, during the session at Jalan Besar Stadium, Bruno Guimarães took full part in ball work for the first time this week, lining up in midfield alongside Andrey Santos and Rayan. In goal, following the rotation plan established by goalkeeping coach Taffarel, Pedro Morisco has emerged as the leading option to start the match. Ancelotti's starting lineup featured Wesley, Jair, Gabriel Magalhães and Douglas Santos in defense, with an attacking trio of Estêvão, Raphinha and Vinicius Júnior. However, the coach left the battle for the left-back spot open. According to ge, Inter Milan's Carlos Augusto spent more time with the starters during training, leaving it unclear whether he or Douglas Santos will get the nod. To fine-tune the attack's movement, Ancelotti held an 11-against-zero tactical drill, with no opposition. In this exercise, Rayan moved through the central channel behind Raphinha, tasked with exploiting open spaces to finish moves inside the penalty area. With potential changes during the match in mind, the coaching staff also tested Marlon Gomes, Gabriel Bontempo and João Gomes in the first team. The Shakhtar Donetsk player was assessed in both holding and central midfield roles. Brazil face Japan this Saturday at 7:15 a.m. Brasília time at Singapore's National Stadium. item.title: ‘A league without emotion’: Hugo Cuypers opens up on why he left the MLS for Monterrey and Mexican football
item.description: ‘A league without emotion’: Hugo Cuypers opens up on why he left the MLS for Monterrey and Mexican football Hugo Cuypers has earned himself a first call up to the Belgian national team . The 29-year-old striker has been in fine form over the past few seasons, starting with his 51 goals for Gent in 90 games. In 2024 he left Belgian football to play in the MLS with Chicago Fire. Again, Cuypers was prolific, scoring 44 goals in 82 games. Yet this past summer he left the MLS and, in an interview with HLN , was hardly the biggest advocate for the league. Of the league, Cuypers said ‘ A league without emotion. Until the playoffs, it feels like you are only playing friendly matches. Whether you win or lose, it doesn’t really matter. Football is not a priority there ‘. With his side then deciding to sign Polish legend Robert Lewandowski to start the season, clearly Cuypers felt that his time was up. However, Cuypers could have stayed in the league if he wanted to. He revealed that there were offers from other MLS clubs to keep him in the league, hardly surprising given his record for Chicago Fire. However, Cuypers did not enjoy the league or the mindset of the owners. The 29-year-old said ‘ You have 25 clubs there that believe they will become champions because they have rich owners. But actually, they don’t even know how to win. Look, I struggled with that American mindset. That is why I turned down all offers from MLS clubs this summer ‘. What the MLS was to Cuypers is clearly contrasted starkly by his new club. Cuypers crossed the border into Mexico to join Monterrey, where he already has nine goals in 20 games. Unlike the MLS, Cuypers feels that football is a real priority in Mexico. Passionate fans and the level is what Cuypers decided was more important than what the MLS could offer, while also giving him a greater chance of making it into the Belgian set up under Mark van Bommel. That decision has certainly paid off for the striker. Speaking on his experience so far in Mexico, Cuypers said ‘ The atmosphere is incredible. There are a lot of red cards – they really go in recklessly over there – but the general level is better than in America ‘. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: Kendrick Perkins noticed something about Lebron James vs Celtics for the ‘first time’ ever
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James was found wanting in the Philadelphia 76ers’ marquee game against the Boston Celtics, and Kendrick Perkins noticed something for the first time ever. In what was billed as a fight of the elites, the Boston Celtics dominated en route to a 123-101 win against the Philadelphia 76ers. LeBron James scored just 11 points on an ugly shooting night where he connected just one of his 3PT attempts, finishing with a +/- of -17. His teammates weren’t much better, but James’ performances had Kendrick Perkins noticing something for the very first time. Kendrick Perkins on LeBron James Usually, these are the kind of games where James’ light shines the brightest and he takes over through sheer talent and mentality. There was nothing of the sort against the Celtics as a much younger and athletic side ran rings around the 76ers and James. It is only one game, and it’s not wise to bet against James because he’s so driven as an athlete, but on the basis of that one game as evidence, count Perkins among doubters. Speaking on ESPN , Perkins said that for the first time, James looked “old” in his career. He said: “LeBron looked old for the first time. No, seriously, for the first time in 20-plus years, he looked old last night. And this is a prime example of why I’ve been begging and pleading for LeBron James to play more of the centre position. If I’m Nick Nurse, I stagger the minutes because it helps LeBron James offensively. LeBron is not just getting by anybody no more. “LeBron wants the mismatches. So now, all of a sudden, you either bring a bigger guy out on him on the perimeter, where he can get by them, or he has a smaller guy on him on the low block. “And you talk about a dynamic roller. LeBron James is still a hell of a screen-and-roll guy. So, if I’m Nick Nurse and I’m trying to figure out this offence, the best way to do it is go small-ball and put LeBron at the five, and then every now and then we see a sprinkle of him and Joel Embiid.” James has been averse to playing centre all his career, but the decision to move him there at this stage of his career isn’t very wise, despite what Perkins suggests. The centres in the modern NBA are athletic as well, and the bruising in addition is something James can do without at his age. If anything, a playmaking point guard role with shooters and runners around him will benefit him more. However, all these conversations based on one bad game are premature anyway. James doesn’t “look old” anymore. He is old, and it’s a testament to his fitness levels that he’s still contributing at such a high level. These games come with the territory at this stage of his career. item.title: Ohio State drops to historic low in CFP rankings
item.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio (WJW) — The Ohio State Buckeyes have hit a new low in the College Football Playoff rankings . Ohio State dropped to No. 20 in the latest CFP rankings released Tuesday, Nov. 10, marking the program's lowest position since the playoff rankings began in 2014. 2 Ohio cities rank among America’s best small cities The previous low was No. 16 in the first CFP rankings released on Oct. 26, 2014. The Buckeyes also fell outside the top 12 for the first time since 2017. The latest drop comes after Ohio State suffered its third loss of the season and second straight defeat. The Buckeyes started the season as the nation's No. 1 team, but after quarterback Julian Sayin was injured, Ohio State's season began to unravel. The Buckeyes are now 6-3 overall and 4-2 in Big Ten play. Loved ones mourn 2 women killed in wrong-way crash on I-90: ‘Horrible tragedy’ Ohio State remains mathematically eligible for the 12-team playoff field. The ranking also puts another streak in jeopardy. Ohio State and Alabama are the only two programs to appear in every CFP ranking since the system began. The Buckeyes host Northwestern Saturday. item.title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013 For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking , consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one. The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December Ashworth departed only five months after joining. Continue reading...

item.title: The biggest CFB salary ever, plus MLB offseason clues
item.description: The Pulse Newsletter 📣 | This is The Athletic’s daily sports newsletter. Sign up here to receive The Pulse directly in your inbox. Good morning! Look for some clues today. Coming up: 🖋️ Small deal, big implications 💰 Kamario’s dollars 👀 Pep to USMNT? Dylan Buell / Getty Images Baseball offseasons, particularly of late, have been defined by patience. item.title: Harry Kane’s England caps record: an illustrious career in numbers and charts
item.description: Striker to play historic 126th match and that’s far from the only statistic that sets him apart for his country Harry Kane will become the most capped player for England’s men when he features against Croatia at Wembley. Yet in the context of the grand history of international football, his record total will be relatively low. Kane will draw level with players including Dani Alves, Eden Hazard and Paolo Maldini on 126 caps. Illustrious players, none of whom lead their country’s appearance standings. Neither do Kevin De Bruyne or Luís Figo, on 127, or Manuel Neuer with 128. It will be some time next year before England’s captain enters European football’s top 50 players for international caps, never mind the global standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?
item.description: Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino. The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era. Continue reading...

In a letter sent to players explaining the decision, the US Soccer Federation cited safety concerns for players and staff, referring them to the US state department’s travel advisory for Qatar, which encourages citizens to reconsider travel to the country “due to risk of armed conflict” and asks government employees to obtain special authorization to do so. “Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament,” US Soccer’s letter to players reads. “The wellbeing of our players and staff will always be our top priority. item.title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper
item.description: It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’ A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino. If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Tuchel keeps laser focus on ‘unfinished business’ with England
item.description: Head coach did not insert release clause into contract Tuchel ‘open to everything’ including staying after Euros Thomas Tuchel will not be going anywhere before Euro 2028. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to leave his role as the USA men’s head coach to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United , but Tuchel has not lost his passion for international football and has revealed he did not insert a release clause when he extended his deal as England’s manager this year. It will not matter whether there is an approach from a big club before the next tournament. United can pay about £7m to get Pochettino out of his deal, but the Football Association does not have to worry about being forced to let Tuchel go. “There’s no intention [of leaving],” Tuchel said. “I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.” Continue reading...

item.title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
item.description: Team must win World Cup group to trigger rule Spain, US, Germany and England currently in top four The top four ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, ­provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa. Spain, USA, Germany and England are ranked one to four in the world respectively, although USA and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on the 7 December updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An eternal shame’: Bilic and Croatia aim to use 7-0 humbling as fuel against England
item.description: The home humiliation last month has left a scar on Croatian football but their manager wants them to use it to positive effect in the Wembley rematch As Croatia prepare to face England at Wembley on Thursday in the Nations League, wounds from a humiliating defeat by the same opponents last month are fresh and there is a lingering feeling of unease. No one will say it – certainly not Slaven Bilic, who always believes in achieving goals that may seem unreachable to most others – but the impression is that Croatia would be satisfied to accept another defeat, provided it was gentle enough by score and hard‑fought by approach; that this game is not so much about the points as the (self-)respect they can regain. Continue reading...

item.title: League One clubs aim for further curbs on spending as budgets continue to spiral
item.description: Wage bills in third tier have increased by 15% this season ‘Luxury tax’ and three-year limits on losses considered League One clubs want to introduce new spending restrictions to reduce losses by limiting investment from owners. Clubs in the division voted to tighten the rules last summer by reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover, and removed a staggered approach to owner investment, so that only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the rest assigned to infrastructure projects. Less than six months later many want to go further. Continue reading...

item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. Continue reading...

item.title: Is No 10 still the best, or No 41? The myths and maths of Premier League shirt numbers
item.description: While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not. That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes. Continue reading...

item.title: Bone broth, sweets ban and acupuncture: Harry Kane’s road to record England cap
item.description: Obsessive attention to detail is helping striker to reach new heights – and a 126th international appearance on Thursday It was Harry Kane’s dirty little secret. Something the England captain got up to after matches. He felt he deserved the indulgence. Yes, it can be revealed, Kane loved to reward himself after a gruelling 90 minutes with a bag of sweets. “I do like a Haribo,” he said with a smile after the Nations League win against Czechia in Prague at the end of September. No more. At the beginning of last season, Kane took the decision to cut out the naughty treats. After a while, he noticed a difference. He felt sharper; able to sprint more, make a greater number of accelerations. Was it down to this latest entry on the list of personal sacrifices? Or was it a consequence of his broader health regime, the scope of which is mind-blowing? Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | ‘Where the hell is Roy Keane!’ Fifty shades of great football debate
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Forget about Michael Carrick. Don’t dwell on Women’s Bigger Cup. Fret not about Pierre Sage. No, the big football story of the day is Big Website’s Ultimate 1-50 , a rundown of the male footballers best associated with each squad number. It’s lighthearted reading designed to entertain, maybe even inform, and perhaps spark a few memories and a touch of debate. Or, if you prefer, a rage-bait waste of time that shames the internet. Where the hell is Roy Keane! How dare you leave out Bobby Moore! And Pelé? A list without Pelé? I don’t want to live in a world where there are lists without Pelé. Such is the world these days, though surely a certain amount of respect is due to an exercise that shuns Lionel Messi and Zinedine Zidane but can welcome in Salvatore Sirigu and Mateusz Klich. And true, it might be a challenging read for those (and, let’s be clear, we’re absolutely definitely not referring to ourselves here, no sirree) old enough to have been brought up in an era of 1; 2, 5, 6, 3; 7, 4, 8, 11; 9 (big man), 10 (little man). The days of two substitutes who wore Nos 12 and 14. The days of a quarter of wine gums in your pocket and misty rain drifting across the floodlights and … oh my god Asamoah Gyan is wearing No 3 and playing up front. This is not a drill. Repeat this is not a drill. Burn it all down, the game’s gone. There is something about it all that does invoke strangely strong reactions, but every day is a school day. So, yes, there remains a hallowed aura around 1-11 but even some of the game’s greats – we’re looking at you Gerd Müller and Johan Cruyff – are best associated with numbers outside of the traditional undectet. And, as Jonathan Wilson brilliantly illustrates here , there’s a risk of being a bit Eurocentric when it comes to numbering – Argentina’s tactical evolution, for example, meant their traditional back four lines up 4, 2, 6, 3, with the No 5 in central midfield. Brazil too has No 5 as the defensive midfielder, with the standard back four as 4, 2, 3, 6. And don’t get us started on Hungary at Wembley in 1953 – Nandor Hidegkuti, you rascal! So do yourself a favour and dig into today’s offering. You might learn something. Or you might just get really, really cross about Curtis Jones. Either way, it’s win-win. Appreciate it’s all highly subjective but quite how you can give the all-time No 17 shirt to Kevin De Bruyne without so much as a mention of the legendary Pelly Ruddock Mpanzu is beyond me. What other player has gone from non-league to Premier League with the same club ? OK, it’s a bit niche but a far more worthy winner in my completely unbiased (honest guv) opinion” – Kev Goddard. All this talk of 4-4 draws ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) is very intoxicating for Chesterfield fans of a certain vintage. First up, the 1992 draw at Anfield where we threw away a 4-1 lead after a Liverpool comeback inspired by Istvan Kozma (no, really). Dave Lancaster scored two that night a

item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. Continue reading...

item.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
item.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure. *** Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. The flamin’ pitch drop experiment began in 1930 and is designed to demonstrate how an apparent solid (pitch) behaves like an extremely viscous liquid. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. Without the need for intercontinental travel, perhaps other readers can now appreciate what it’s like to watch Arsenal win 1-0 ” – John Holtom. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
item.description: John Aloisi’s players need a point on the final day to seal their maiden title – but their form has dropped off a cliff With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic. The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. Continue reading...

item.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: managers sacked after signing new deals, war victims commemorated on kits and the first club website (part II) Mail us with all of your questions and answers It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women. Continue reading...

item.title: From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas. “I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Continue reading...

item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Barney Ronay
item.content:encoded: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
